Context: The quotations below are from Denys, a British officer serving in the British Indian Army in `1947`, who was interviewed as part of the “Partition Voices” project.
Content: “We were fairly thin on the ground by `text(August 1947)`. On Independence `text(Day)` I was in Lahore making my way back to England. I remember people shaking my hand saying, 'Thank you. Thank you for making us independent.'
“The station was knee-deep in bodies. It was a terrible time. Trains coming from `text(one)` direction full of dead Sikhs and Hindus— and trains coming from the other full of dead Muslims.
“We all— sort of people like myself, British officers— felt Partition went through too fast. The whole thing was not thought through.
“I think the British government of the `text(day)` was anxious to get it done quickly. It was a great mistake.”
